settings.title: Settings
settings.about.appearance: Choose the app theme, the interface style and the code surface. Low-risk preferences are saved immediately.
settings.about.voice: Configure voice input and Live Voice in one place.
settings.about.agent: How much the agent may do without asking, and what it is allowed to reach.
settings.about.model: Which ternary pack runs on this machine, and where its weights live.
settings.about.reasoning: The sampler set the engine is launched with. The GGUF carries only temperature, top-k and top-p.
settings.section.code.desc: Choose code themes, font size, and display options independently from the interface font size.
settings.section.sampling.desc: These edit the {{mode}} profile; the other one keeps its own values.
settings.row.themeMode.desc: Choose light, dark, or follow the system theme.
settings.row.terminalTheme.desc: Follow the interface theme, or keep the appearance selected in the terminal.
settings.row.builtInBrowser: Use the built-in browser for terminal links
settings.row.builtInBrowser.desc: When off, HTTP and HTTPS links open in your system default browser.
settings.row.language.desc: The catalog every label in the app is read from.
settings.row.fontStyle.desc: The interface typeface. Code always stays monospaced.
settings.row.contentWidth.desc: Adjust the maximum width of task content and the composer.
settings.row.fileIcons.desc: Choose the file icon style used by task text and inline file references.
settings.row.glass.desc: Controls dialog mask blur, glass layers, and similar visual effects. Turn off to use solid backgrounds.
settings.row.appIconRoll.desc: Draw one of the twelve when the app opens. Choosing a tile above keeps that one instead, and turning this off keeps the icon the app is wearing now.
settings.row.lightCodeTheme.desc: Highlighting theme used for code content in the light interface.
settings.row.darkCodeTheme.desc: Highlighting theme used for code content in the dark interface.
settings.row.showLineNumbers.desc: Display line numbers in code and diff views.
settings.row.uiFontSize.desc: Adjust interface text without changing icons or layout dimensions.
settings.row.codeFontSize.desc: Adjust the default font size for code blocks, file previews, and diff views.
settings.row.inputDevice.desc: Choose the microphone for voice input, or follow the current system device automatically.
settings.row.voiceInput.desc: Use the microphone for voice input in the current task composer.
settings.row.recognitionPolish.desc: Clean up pauses, repetition, and punctuation so transcripts are ready to send.
settings.row.voiceprint.desc: Use voice characteristics from the start of each recording to reduce nearby speech.
settings.row.sendAutomatically.desc: With the DJI Mic Mini 2 collaboration kit, press once to start recording and again to stop and send.
settings.row.corrections.desc: Add proper names or terminology to improve recognition accuracy.
settings.row.liveVoiceShortcut.desc: Start Live Voice in the currently focused task composer, or end the active Live Voice task.
settings.row.approvalMode.desc: Reads and workspace edits run on their own; anything that leaves the machine asks first.
settings.row.shellTimeout.desc: A command still running after this long is stopped.
settings.row.compressAt.desc: Share of the model window after which older turns are summarized into a “Context compressed” divider.
settings.row.keepRecentTurns.desc: Recent turns, plus every open file, are kept verbatim.
settings.row.allowRemote.desc: Off: the app talks only to the engine on this machine, and the Local badge says so too.
settings.row.telemetry.desc: Nothing in this build collects or sends usage data, so there is nothing here to switch.
settings.row.packing.desc: Which quantization the engine loads. Auto probes Metal, CUDA, Vulkan or CPU and picks the best viable pack.
settings.row.modelDir.desc: Where the GGUF packs are stored on this machine.
settings.row.hfTokenEnv.desc: The name of an environment variable holding a read-only token for the gated repo. The token itself is never stored.
settings.row.offloadAllLayers.desc: Keep every layer resident on the accelerator. Off leaves the remainder on the CPU.
settings.row.flashAttention.desc: Fused attention kernels, where the selected backend supports them.
settings.row.visionLazyLoad.desc: Only pay for the vision tower when a message carries an image.
settings.row.dedicatedServerSlots.desc: Run the server with one slot and a bounded prompt cache, so the cache does not thrash across requests.
settings.row.effort.desc: Auto takes the effort the selected model publishes as its default. Low reasons about as long as Extra high: the chat template only accepts xhigh, medium and none.
settings.row.nonThinking.desc: Sample with the instruct profile. The model's measured quality comes from thinking mode.
settings.row.maxTokens.desc: A cap that is too small ends the run mid-thought and yields an empty reply.
settings.row.contextTokens.desc: Tokens the server reserves. The model's full window is 262144.
settings.row.temperature.desc: Model card: 1.0 in thinking mode, 0.7 in instruct.
settings.row.minP.desc: Floor relative to the best candidate. The GGUF carries no value for it, so the launcher always passes one.
settings.row.presencePenalty.desc: Also absent from the file, so it comes from here.
settings.row.repetitionPenalty.desc: Applied by the launcher rather than the GGUF header.
settings.row.systemPrompt.desc: The instruction every run starts from.
settings.voice.pending: Recording starts once the local engine is installed. These preferences are stored now.
settings.help.title: What is running
notice.effort-not-supported: {{model}} accepts reasoning effort {{accepted}}; the saved choice "{{chosen}}" is not among them, so this server replies at "{{sent}}". Settings › Reasoning can change it.
notice.engine-restarted:
The engine stopped between runs, so it is being started again (restart {{attempt}} of {{max}}). Its last lines:
{{log}}
notice.tool-call-without-tools: The model asked for a tool ({{name}}). This prompt went out with the composer's Coding control off, so nothing was read and the answer is from the model alone. Press it and ask again to have the workspace actually looked at.
notice.tool-not-offered: The model asked for {{name}}, which this build does not have: it offers four reads of the workspace and one edit inside it — read_file, list_dir, glob, grep_search and edit_file — and reaches nothing outside.
notice.tool-loop-capped: The model asked for tools {{rounds}} times in a row without answering, so the run stopped there and its last tool result stands. What you see is the beginning of the answer, not the end. Narrower wording usually gets it to answer in one pass.
notice.prompt-too-long: This prompt is {{tokens}} tokens on the server's own count, and the window is {{window}} wide, so the model will not see all of it: it answers from the end of what it was given, with the beginning dropped before it reaches the model. Shorten the message, or raise Context window in Settings if the machine has the room.
notice.context-trimmed: This conversation has outgrown the context window, so the server could not replay all of it: the model answered from the most recent turns, with the earliest ones dropped before it saw them. Start a new task to answer from a clean window, or raise Context window in Settings if the machine has the room.
notice.budget-exhausted: The reply hit its {{maxTokens}} token cap, so it is cut off. Raise Maximum tokens per reply in Settings if the answer needs more room.
notice.not-filed: This conversation was not filed, so it will not be in the sidebar once the window closes: {{why}}
notice.model-takes-no-images: {{model}} publishes no vision projector, so there is no file this app could start it with to make it read pictures — it answers text alone. A picture needs a model whose card ships one, such as Bonsai 2 4B.
notice.projector-absent: {{model}} can read pictures, but {{file}} — the file that makes it able to — is not in this machine's models directory, so this run stopped before the model saw the picture. Downloading this model's weights fetches it.
notice.projector-loading: A picture needs a server that was started with its vision projector, so the engine is being restarted with {{file}} loaded. The wait is the model coming back up, not the answer.
blocker.engine-not-installed.title: The engine isn't on this machine yet
blocker.engine-not-installed.detail: SmoLLM Studio runs models with one specific build of llama.cpp, and this machine doesn't have it yet. Installing it fetches exactly the build this app was pinned to — nothing else is chosen for you.
blocker.stock-engine-rejected.title: This model can't run on standard llama.cpp
blocker.stock-engine-rejected.detail: The llama.cpp on this machine is the standard one, which can't read these weights. Installing the build this app pins is what fixes it; the app will never quietly fall back to a build that answers wrongly.
blocker.weights-not-downloaded.title: The model file hasn't been downloaded yet
blocker.weights-not-downloaded.detail: {{file}} hasn't been downloaded yet, and nothing can run without it.
blocker.integrity-mismatch.title: The model file isn't the one that was published
blocker.integrity-mismatch.detail: {{file}} isn't byte-for-byte the file that was published, so the app won't load it — an interrupted download is the usual cause. Downloading it again clears this.
blocker.rotation-metadata-missing.title: This file wasn't exported by Prism
blocker.rotation-metadata-missing.detail: This file came from somewhere other than the official Prism release, and a ternary model without its rotation settings answers confidently and wrongly rather than failing loudly. Get the file from the model's own page.
blocker.engine-pin-too-old.title: The pinned engine build has no downloadable files
blocker.engine-pin-too-old.detail: The engine build this app is pinned to was published without any files to download, so there is nothing here the app can fetch. Moving the pin to the next build that ships binaries clears this.
sidebar.knowledgeAbout: Browse the model catalog and this machine's copies of it
sidebar.extensionsAbout: The tools the agent is offered, and which of them this build runs
knowledge.title: Knowledge Center
knowledge.machine.about: What the catalog pins, and which of those files sit on this machine.
knowledge.loadFailed: The catalog could not be read: {{error}}
knowledge.packs.desc: Each packing the catalog pins for this model, and whether this machine holds its file.
knowledge.vision.desc: The projector files this model's card publishes for image input — a separate file, fetched alongside one of the packs above.
knowledge.vision.none: The card publishes no projector for this model
knowledge.vision.note: The engine takes a projector at launch when one is asked for, and the composer's attach button is what asks: attaching a picture starts the server with this file loaded, so the first picture after a text-only run also pays a reload.
knowledge.issues.desc: Quoted from the model card. Nothing here checks these conditions against this machine.
knowledge.engine.desc: The single llama.cpp build this app is allowed to run.
knowledge.engine.pinned.desc: The tag the lock file names. Installing fetches that tag and nothing else.
knowledge.engine.state.desc: Whether the pinned build's binary is actually in the app's engine directory.
knowledge.held.desc: {{gb}} GB of the catalog's files sit in that directory.
knowledge.sizeNote: Sizes are the figures the catalog pins, counted from the packs marked present — not a scan of the disk.
extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.loadFailed: The tool registry could not be read: {{error}}
extensions.about: This app installs no add-ons, so the row's local meaning is the other thing that lives in that place: the capabilities the model is handed when it is allowed to act.
extensions.runs.desc: {{count}} tools reach an executor: a call to one is confined to the workspace root named at the left, and its result is replayed into the next request. The two labels on the right are the class of the call, and what the approval dial in force would do with it.
extensions.declaredOnly.desc: {{count}} tools the agent is offered and this build has no executor for. The transcript still opens a row for the call; the row is where it stops.
extensions.note: Both columns are the host's own answer. The classes come from the registry a run is built from, and the right-hand label comes from the policy engine that decides a call mid-run — so this list moves with the approval dial and the privacy switch in Settings, and cannot read more permissive than the agent acts.
